items.title: CVE-2026-112077 | radareorg radare2 6.2.0/6.2.2 HTTP Sandbox Policy libr/core/rtr_http.inc.c r_core_cmd_str_pipe protection mechanism (Issue 26861)
items.author: vuldb.com
items.content: A vulnerability was found in radareorg radare2 6.2.0/6.2.2. It has been classified as problematic. This issue affects the function r_core_cmd_str_pipe in the library libr/core/rtr_http.inc.c of the component HTTP Sandbox Policy Handler. Performing a manipulation results in protection mechanism failure. This vulnerability is known as CVE-2026-112077. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. No exploit is available. Upgrading the affected component is recommended. The pre-requisite of the vulnerability is reflected by the CVSS vector. One of the project maintainers explains: "There is a real sandbox configuration issue here, but the report overstates it. The HTTP server defaults to http.sandbox=true, so commands received through /cmd temporarily enable cfg.sandbox. However, cfg.sandbox.grain defaults to all, which means all sandbox capabilities - including exec - remain allowed. Therefore enabling the HTTP sandbox alone does NOT prevent commands from spawning processes. This only matters when the HTTP command endpoint is reachable by someone you do not trust. It is not a remote vulnerability by default: the HTTP server must first be started and exposed to the attacker."

items.title: CVE-2026-111874 | OpenCATS 0.10.0 Career Portal CareersUI.php processLogin applyToJobSubAction excessive authentication (Issue 905)
items.author: vuldb.com
items.content: A vulnerability has been found in OpenCATS 0.10.0 and classified as problematic. Affected is the function processLogin of the file modules/careers/CareersUI.php of the component Career Portal. This manipulation of the argument applyToJobSubAction causes improper restriction of excessive authentication attempts. This vulnerability is registered as CVE-2026-111874. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. Furthermore, an exploit is available. It is suggested to install a patch to address this issue. The project maintainer explains: "Candidates will now need to authenticate each time they access the Career Portal and successfully complete the CAPTCHA as part of that authentication flow. The authenticated candidate identity is now maintained server-side rather than relying on the previous persistent client-side cats…cw cookie mechanism. Application-level rate limiting is deliberately not in scope for this change. In my view, request throttling and brute-force protection of that kind are better applied at the network, reverse-proxy or web-server layer, where they can be configured appropriately for each deployment without OpenCATS having to implement and maintain its own rate-limiting framework. I'll update the online documentation to that effect."
